rows.title_short: Enhancing The Discount On The Purchase Of Goods And Services Of Senior Citizens And Persons With Disabilities
rows.abstract:
Seeks to grant senior citizens and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) a twenty percent (20%) discount and exemption from value-added tax, or the special discount on purchase of basic necessities and prime commodities, in addition to any prevailing promotional offers or discounts extended by business establishments.
Aims to clarify that the discounts for senior citizens and PWDs shall be treated as part of deductible expense of business establishments.

rows.author: C102;J127;J014;K099;I109;J093;K140;K080;G050;J125;H057;I041;K079;F057;K061;I070;K008;I091;K123;K026;K048;K125;K025;F076;K104;K023;K073;K074;
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES OF SENIOR CITIZENS AND PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES
rows.title_short: Rationalizing The Benefits And Privileges Of Senior Citizens And Persons With Disabilities
rows.abstract:
Seeks to consolidate benefits and rationalize existing provisions in the laws governing the rights and privileges of senior citizens and persons with disabilities for them to enjoy adequate social services, decent standard of living, and improved quality of life.
Provides for the following privileges for senior citizens and persons with disabilities: a.) Twenty percent (20%) discount and exemption from the value-added tax (VAT) on goods and services, as provided under Section 4 of RA 7432 or the “Senior Citizens Act” as amended, and Section 32 of RA 7277 of the “Magna Carta for Persons with Disability,” as amended; b.) Special discount on purchase of basic commodities, which shall be applied on the final price of the goods or services after promotional offer or discount extended by business establishments; c.) Twenty percent (20%) discount and exemption from the VAT on the utilization of transportation services, including the payment of parking fees and the use of expressway and skyways; d.) Grant of fifteen percent (15%) discount on the monthly utilization of water and electricity supplied by public utilities applied on the first 100 kWh of electricity consumption and 30 cubic meters of water consumption per household; e.) Additional deduction from gross income of employers of senior citizens and persons with disabilities, equivalent to twenty-five percent (25%) of the total amount paid as salaries and wages; and f.) Exemption from fees on training for socioeconomic programs by government agencies.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2024-05-21, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-05-22 and received by the Senate on 2024-05-22

rows.title_full:
AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 134 AND 168 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE
KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the issue that Sec.134 and Sec. 168 of the NIRC as amended were not synchronized by R.A. 10351 (Sin Tax Law of 2012) and later laws, but are still anchored to the old system of taxing alcohol as an ingredient.

Proposes the following amendments to NIRC Code of 1997, as amended:

“SEC.134 [Domestic]Denatured Alcohol. - Alcohol of not less than one hundred eighty degrees (180) proof (ninety percent (90%) absolute alcohol) FROM WHATEVER SOURCE INTENDED AS INGREDIENT IN THE MANUFACTURE OF DISTILLED SPIRITS, shall when suitably denatured LOCALLY and rendered unfit for oral intake, be exempt from the excise tax, . . .”

“SEC.168. Denaturing Within Premises. - . . . the process of denaturing alcohol shall effected only within the [distillery] premises OF THE DOMESTIC DISTILLER AND COMPOUNDER OF DISTILLED SPIRITS WITH RECTIFYING FACILITIES . . .”
rows.status: Substituted by HB10535

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ILLICIT TOBACCO TRADE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Defines "Illicit tobacco trade" as any practice or conduct prohibited by law and which relates to the production, shipment, receipt, possession, distribution, sale, or purchase of tobacco products, including vapor products and heated tobacco products, including any practice or conduct intended to facilitate such activity.

Seeks to impose heavy and differentiated penalties based on the degree of involvement in illicit trade; establish a modem digital tracking and tracing system; form an inter-agency body to facilitate information sharing and collaborative enforcement among government agencies and stakeholders; broaden the scope of activities that fall under illicit tobacco trade; and strengthen monitoring by mandating the conduct of regular surveys to determine the size, volume, nature, and conduct of illicit trade. Related terms: electronic cigarette; e-cigarette
rows.status: Substituted by HB11286

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE CRIME OF SUBORDINATION OF PERJURY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "REVISED PENAL CODE"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to add a new Article 184-A to Act No. 3815 to read as follows:

“Article 184-A. Subordination of Perjury. - Whoever procures, coerces, or otherwise induces another to commit any perjury shall suffer the respective penalties provided in this section:Â  Provided, That if the person responsible for the commission of this felony is a public officer or employee, or if the testimony results in the institution of a criminal action against another, the penalty shall be imposed in its maximum period: “ a) a fine not to exceed one million pesos; and b) perpetual absolute disqualification from holding any appointive or elective position in the government . . .”

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AND STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL CYBERSECURITY INTER-AGENCY COMMITTEE CREATED UNDER EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 95 (S.2019), RENAMING IT TO NATIONAL CYBERSECURITY COUNCIL, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the growing challenges posed by cyber threats in the country and provide for the mandatory reporting of data breaches by government institutions and GOCCs.
Proposes to rename the National Cybersecurity Inter-Agency Committee into the National Cybersecurity Council (NCC), which shall be the primary authority responsible for cybersecurity-related matters.
Provides for NCC´s functions, among others:Â  assessment of the country´s cybersecurity vulnerabilities; capacity building in response to cybersecurity threats and emergencies; security protocols´ regular update in the storage, handling, and distribution of all forms of digital and electronic documents and communications; a public-private partnership in the field of information sharing involving cyberattacks, threats and vulnerabilities to cyber threats.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11223, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "UNIVERSAL HEALTHCARE ACT"
rows.abstract:
Proposes to adjust the premium contribution rates for migrant workers and self-earning individuals to a more manageable level based on the income floor.

Seeks to provide PhilHealth more flexibility in the collection of contributions by giving them additional powers to compromise, waive, or release interests or surcharges owed by employers, self-employed individuals, and migrant workers, regardless of the amount.

Proposes to increase the age of PhilHealth dependents to 23 years old; and to authorize the President to suspend or defer contribution increases and/or income floor and income ceiling during national emergencies.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING INSTALLMENT PAYMENT SCHEME ON BASIC UTILITY BILLS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
“Three-Gives Law”
Seeks to institutionalize a three (3) equal monthly installment payment scheme on basic utility bills, including electric, water, internet, cable, and telephone bills, upon an official declaration of a State of Calamity.
Proposes a moratorium in the payment or collection of all residential utility bills and prohibits holders of public utility franchises and all service providers from exacting payment or from disconnecting the service due to non-payment within such period.
Proposes that in the case of electric cooperatives, there shall be a moratorium in the payment or collection to government instrumentalities during the entire duration of a state of calamity.
